         Introduction
McElhanney Consulting Services Ltd (McElhanney) was retained by the Diamond Improvement District
(Diamond) to complete a Water System Evaluation study to summarize the condition of the existing water
system and plan for future improvements.



The tasks for this study include:

        1)   Topographic Survey,
        2)   Drawing of Existing Water System,
        3)   Drawing with Watermain Upgrades,
        4)   Class C Cost Estimate,
        5)   Development Potential Discussion,
        6)   Funding Options, and
        7)   Submission of this report.

The results of this Water System Evaluation study are summarized in the following sections of this report.



         Background
The Diamond Improvement District is located directly north of the Town of Ladysmith, BC. This unincorporated
community lies within the Cowichan Valley Reginal District and forms part of Electoral Area “H”. The district
borders the Stz’uminus First Nation to the North and the Town of Ladysmith to the south. The water system
serves a population of approximately 530 residents.

The Diamond Improvement District Waterworks District was incorporated under the Water Act in 1953 and is an
Improvement District as defined under the Local Government Act. The District’s Letters patent was created in
April 21, 1953 and states: “the objects of the improvement district shall be the provision of fire protection and
the acquisition, maintenances, and operation of works buildings, and equipment for that purpose.” The
Proclamation, Letter Patent, and modifications are included in Appendix A for reference.

    Existing System

         Water Supply
The Diamond Improvement District receives water from the Town of Ladysmith through a Water Services
Agreement. The Town of Ladysmith water system has two sources: Stocking Lake and Holland Lake. Water
from both sources is piped directly to the enclosed Arbutus Reservoir where it is chlorinated and distributed by
gravity to the entire Ladysmith service area. Diamond is connected to the Ladysmith water system at two
points:

    1. Rock Creek Road at Gladden Road, and

    2. Christie Road at 3rd Avenue.

Diamond’s water distribution network consists of watermains, hydrants, valves, and services. Watermains are
composed primarily of asbestos-cement (AC) pipe with some polyvinyl chlorine (PVC) pipe. The existing water
system is illustrated on Figure 1, appended to this report.

        Water System Configuration
The District’s water distribution system has two main loops and several linear sections with dead-ends. Looped
watermains provide system redundancy and reduce headloss associated with long dead-end lines. The
Diamond water distribution system benefits from having two connections to the Ladysmith water system. This
provides added backup and security if one supply connection fails.



        Pressure Distribution
System pressure is controlled by pressure reducing valves (PRVs) located at the two points of connection to
the Town of Ladysmith distribution network. Pressure varies throughout the system in proportion to ground
elevation. Highest pressures are at the bottom of the system while the lowest pressures are at the top end of
the system.

The Diamond Improvement District performs annual hydrant inspections. A copy of the two previous inspection
reports in included in Appendix B for reference. The hydrant tests include pressure readings. A summary of
those readings is provided in Figure 2. The minimum and maximum pressures recorded are presented in

Minimum Pipe Sizes

The MMCD Guidelines specify a minimum pipe diameter of 200mm. This minimum size can be reduced to
150mm in residential areas for lengths less than 500m and in looped systems where fire flow requirements can
be met.



        Asbestos Cement Pipe
Asbestos Cement pipe was in common use prior to the introduction of Polyvinyl Chloride in the mid 1970’s.
Since that time many communities have experienced problems with deterioration and the eventual failure of
their AC pipe system. These problems result from a combination of the following factors:

           Failures are most prevalent in districts that use a surface water supply that tends to be slightly
            more acidic than ground water. This ‘soft’ water attacks the cement and reduces pipe strength.
           AC pipe is a brittle material that is prone to cracking when subjected to uneven loads caused by
            trench settlement, slope movement or vehicle loads.
           Insufficient bedding during installation may result in point loads against the outside of the pipe that
            result in high stress and pipe failure.

Many communities in BC have adopted an AC pipe replacement program to spread the cost of upgrades over
time. The warrant for action is assessed on a case by case basis depending on factors specific to the
community.

          Dead-Ends

required. Hydrants may serve as blow-offs where approved by local authority.

       Water-Meter Based Payments
Please note, water meters are installed on all services throughout the Diamond water system. Prior to June
2016, Diamond water users payed a bulk fee for the water consumed. Starting in June 2016, the payment
changed to be based on the individual water meter readings. Water meter-based payments typically decreases
consumption by at least 25%2.



        Unaccounted Water
The Diamond Improvement District advised McElhanney that bulk meter readings (water supply from
Ladysmith) has been compared to the total water consumed per individual meters. This analysis indicated that
the volume of water consumed is within 10% of the bulk meter readings. This is comparable to new and well
managed systems. The amount of water that is lost or unaccounted for can be as high as 50% in older and
poorly managed systems3.

The Diamond Improvement District also records the consumption at both bulk meters on a weekly basis. This
provides a good check to noted if a significant break has occurred within the system.

Maximum Population and Build-Out Timeframe

In summary, it is estimated that the Diamond Improvement District can grow by 58 dwellings. At an average of
2.2 persons/dwelling that is 127 people for a maximum population of 657 people. Assuming 2% annual growth
rate, the full buildout could occur in 11 years (2027). At the current average consumption rate of 243 L/c/day,
the full buildout demand will be 58,000 m3/year which is less than the Water Services Agreement of
70,000 m3/year.

         Fire Flows
The District’s Letters Patent include “the provision of fire protection.” The British Columbia Building Code
references the following documents for fire flow calculations:

           “Needed Fire Flow Guide,” Insurance Services Office
           “NFPA 1142 Standard for Water Supplies for Rural and Suburban Fire Fighting,” National Fire
            Protection Association, 2017
           “Distribution Requirements for Fire Protection,” American Water Works Association (AWWA)

Required fire flows vary with building size, type of construction, and type of occupancy, and exposure to nearby
hazards (other buildings within 15m). A summary of the applicable fire flow standards is presented in Table 3-5
below.

Table 3-4 – MMCD Fire Flow Standards
 MMCD Standard                                              Value

 Minimum Fire Flow                                                                 60 L/s

 Velocity                                                                         3.5 m/s

 Pressure                                                                     150 kPa (22 psi)



Estimated Minimum Fire Flow Demand

The estimated minimum fire flow demand for Diamond is calculated as follows:

           Average Day Demand (ADD):                 243 L/c/day x 530 people = 128,900 L/day or 90 L/min
           Maximum Day Demand (MDD):                 2 (assumed factor) x ADD = 2 x 90 L/min = 180 L/min
           Minimum Fire Flow (MFF):                  60 L/s or 3,600 L/min
           Minimum Fire Flow Demand =                Fire Flow + Domestic Consumption
                                                      = 3,600 L/min + 180 L/min = 3,780 L/min

Pressure Losses at Minimum Fire Flow Demand

At high flows, pressure loss increases as pipe size decreases. A summary of the relative headloss at the Fire
Flow Demand for a section of 100m pipe is summarized in the Table 3-6 below:

Table 3-5 – Headloss at Fire Flow Demand for 100m Pipe
   Diameter                              Headloss                              Velocity
   mm                                    kPa (psi)                             m/s
                 100                             5.4 kPa (61psi)                              8.0

                 150                            0.71 kPa (8.0 psi)                            3.6

                 200                            0.17 kPa (2.0 psi)                            2.0



The above table illustrates the sensitivity of pressure loss to pipe size and the need for watermains to be larger
than 100mm diameter. Take, for example, the section of 477m length of 100mm AC pipe on Christie Road
between the looped highway crossing and the western extents near Arroyo Road. The headloss for the fire
flow demand is estimated to be 477m/100m x 61 psi = 291 psi. The static pressure per the hydrant flow tests is
approximately 96 psi. Therefore, there is not enough pressure in the system to supply the headloss required
for the fire flow. The pipe size should be increased to a minimum 150mm diameter which would occur a
headloss of 477m/100m x 8.0psi = 38 psi. The reduction in pressure for this system would be 96 psi less 38
psi or 39 psi which is substantially above the minimum 20 psi requirement.

   Conclusions
A summary of conclusions is presented below:

       1)  61% or 4,704 m of the district’s watermain are composed of asbestos-cement pipe.
       2)  100mm diameter pipe is smaller than current standards and cannot convey required fire flows.
       3)  Residual pressures range from 421 kPa (61 psi) to 800 kPa (116 psi) and may vary substantially.
       4)  Individual pressure reducing valves are required in all areas with a residual pressure greater than
           515 kPa (75 psi). This applies to all areas of the district except Grouhel Road.
       5) The system currently serves approximately 530 people and is projected to grow to a maximum
           build-out population of 657.
       6) A watermain break in 2016 resulted in the loss of 16,601m3 of water.
       7) Average daily water consumption is 243 litres per capita per day. This consumption is lower than
           other jurisdictions;
       8) Water meter-based billings began in June 2016 and per capita consumption is anticipated to be
           even lower in the future.
       9) There is less than 10% water loss in the system.
       10) Maximum build-out demand is estimated to be 58,000 m3 per year.
       11) System condition and losses are undefined. It is not known if the condition AC pipe is adequate or
           if there are any leaks in the district system.

    Recommendations
Based on our review of the existing information provided, we recommend the following system improvements.
Each project has been assigned a schedule of priority focused on strengthening the system to improve
domestic water supply and improve residential fire flows.

Project 1 – Water Network Flow Assessment & Modeling (Priority 1-5 years)

It is recommended to complete a water network flow assessment and model for the Diamond Improvement
District to:

           Assess the system for leaks and identify replacement priorities.
           Identify recommended pipe size improvements
           Model and size watermain looping scenarios.
           Prioritize replacement projects.
           Model the addition of pressure reduction scenarios (i.e. PRV installations).

Project 2 – 100mm Diameter Watermain Replacement (Priority 1-5 years)

Replacing the undersized 100mm watermains is an essential upgrade required to meet fire flow demands. The
most critical pipes are at the highest elevation with the lowest residual pressures. These should be replaced
first followed by the more down-gradient watermains. Watermain improvements include increasing the number
of fire hydrants to meet current standards. Project 1 is required to be completed first in order to size the
watermains and define where appurtenances, such as pressure-reducing valves, may be required.

Project 3 – 150mm AC Condition Assessment (Priority 1-5 years)

AC watermains are approaching the end their expected service life. All systems deteriorate with age and use;
however, performance may not be affected until deterioration is well advanced. The frequency of watermain
breaks like those experienced in 2016 may increase if the condition of the AC pipes has deteriorated. As such,
we recommend the District undertake a condition assessment of the 150mm AC pipe to identify areas that need
pipe replacement.

Project 4 – Watermain Looping (Priority 6-30 years)

There are two options for system looping:

        1) Arroyo Road to Grouhel Road, and
        2) 12556 Trans Canada Highway to Arroyo Road at Christie Road.

These projects would remove significant dead-ends within the Diamond Improvement District.

Project 5 – 150mm Diameter AC Watermain Replacement Program (Priority 6-30 years)

Based on the findings Projects 1 and 3, the District can implement an AC watermain replacement program to
address the aging infrastructure. Due to the large amount of old AC pipe in use, planning should be
undertaken to replace the critical portions of the main. All watermain improvements include increasing the
number of fire hydrants to meet current standards. There is 2,275m of watermain and it is assumed that all AC
pipe will be replaced within 30 years.

    Capital Expenditure Program
The Local Government Act provides all Improvement Districts with several methods to fund Capital Works.
Under Part 17 of the Local Government Act, there are various methods available to finance the costs of works
and services required due to new development. A list of potential charges an improvement district can apply is
presented below along with a paraphrased description.

           Section 698 – Powers that must be exercised by bylaw
            698 (1) (e) An improvement district board may make bylaws for establishing tolls and other
            charges, including charges for capital expenditures, payable to the improvement district, and the
            times of their payment.

           Section 700 – Subdivision servicing requirements
            700 (1) (a) (b) - The improvement district board may require the provision and construction of: a
            water distribution system and a fire hydrant system.

           Section 701 – Requirements for excess or extended services
            701 (2) - An improvement district may require the owner of land that is to be subdivided to provide
            portion of water system that will serve land other than the land being subdivided or developed.

            Section 702 – Latecomer chargers and cost recovery for excess or extended services
           702 (3) – If the improvement district pays all or part of the costs of excess or extended services, it
            may recover costs by a latecomer charge.


In general, these funding options are to fund two different types of projects, those that serve:

           existing customers; and,
           future development.

Funding methods are described further in the following sections.



         Projects Servicing Existing Customers
Renewal Reserve Fund

Renewal Reserve Funds allow a Local District to put money aside to finance the cost of renewing capital
infrastructure. This saving mechanism can reduce or eliminate the amount of borrowing required to construct
future works. Renewal Reserve Funds can be formally established with a bylaw passed by the Board of
Trustees and registered with the Inspector of Municipalities. Funding sources typically include the following:

           Operating surpluses;
           Budgeted annual contributions;
           Miscellaneous revenue items;
           Sale of assets;


                                                                                             2231-31902-01| Page 15

--- Page 20 ---

                                                                                           Water System Evaluation
                                                                                                     April 20, 2017
                                                                                       Diamond Improvement District

Short Term Borrowing

The Board of Trustees is authorized to pass borrowing bylaws as required to meet approved expenditures.
Short term borrowing is typically used to fund unexpected costs and to provide interim financing for capital
projects. Temporary borrowing bylaws are registered with the Inspector of Municipalities and are secured by
the toll and taxing powers of the Waterworks District.

Long Term Borrowing

The Local Government Act allows a Waterworks District to borrow money by issue and sale of notes, bonds
debentures and other securities. In practice this method of borrowing is arranged through the Municipal
Finance Authority and is guaranteed by the Province. Long term borrowing bylaws and associated documents
are prepared by the Ministry of Community, Sport and Cultural Development.



         Projects Serving Future Development
Capital Expenditure Charges

The ability of a Waterworks District to serve future development may be restricted by the system’s capacity to
meet that additional demand. Upgrades to the system that are required to meet this increase in demand, but
are not tied to a single specific development project are typically funded through a Capital Expenditure Charge
(CEC) Fund.

All proposed watermain and fire hydrant upgrades will support future development. The maximum number of
lots is assumed to be 259 or 22% greater than the current number of lots at 201. Therefore, watermain
upgrades can be apportioned 78% to current users and 22% to future users.



Subdivision Regulation Bylaw

Subdivision applications made to the Ministry of Transportation are referred to the Waterworks District for
review and comment. The District’s position to support an application is typically based on capacity available in
the existing system and the ability to service newly created lots. The cost of servicing new development is
typically allocated to the applicant and not existing users.

Waterworks Districts are empowered to pass bylaws that define servicing standards to be met with new
construction and the Approving Officer must not approve a subdivision until services meet those standards.
Servicing Standards typically apply to development as well as subdivision and are subject to the following
limitations:

           Standards can only apply to works that are included in the Letters Patent (waterworks in the case
            of The Diamond Improvement District Waterworks District).
           The landowner is 100% responsible for the cost of works required to meet standards that are built
            on his property and on highway adjacent to his property.




                                                                                           2231-31902-01| Page 16

--- Page 21 ---

                                                                                            Water System Evaluation
                                                                                                      April 20, 2017
                                                                                        Diamond Improvement District

Latecomer Charges

In certain cases, the developer is required to oversize works that are constructed on his property or within
adjacent road right of way, or he may be required to construct works that extend beyond his property to serve
his development. When excess or extended services also benefit adjacent properties, then the developer has
a right to request that the Waterworks District pass a Latecomer’s Bylaw that allows him to recoup his
additional costs.

         Proposed Capital Expenditure Charges
Proposed CEC fees assume that 22% of all proposed works benefit future customers. CECs are typically
distributed based on a per person basis. The maximum buildout calculations estimate an additional 127
people will occupy 41 new Suburban Residential Homes and 17 Mobile Homes. Assuming an occupancy
density of 2.0 persons/household in a Suburban Residential Home, the occupancy for mobile homes is
estimated at 1.5 persons/household. The CEC fees are calculated as follows:

           $   1.49M       Cost of Projects in 5-Year Capital Plan
           $   1.43M       Cost of Projects in 6-30 Year Timeline
           $   2.92M       Total Cost Estimate of proposed projects
           $ 642,000       22% of Total Cost Estimate to CECs
           127             Total new residents
           $ 5054.99       Estimated CEC per person (22% of Total Cost Estimate ÷ Total New Residents)

           $10,109.98      Estimated CEC per Suburban Residential Home (2 x CEC per person)
           $ 7,617.33      Estimated CEC per Mobile Home (1.5 x CEC per person)

                               WATER SERVICES AGREEMENT

THIS AGREEMENT is dated for reference the 1st day of July, 2016.

BETWEEN:

                 TOWN OF LADYSMITH, a municipal corporation incorporated
                 under the Local Government Act, PO Box 220, 410 Esplanade,
                 Ladysmith, British Columbia, V9G 1A2

                 (“Ladysmith”)

AND:

                 DIAMOND IMPROVEMENT DISTRICT, an improvement
                 district incorporated under the Local Government Act, Box 747,
                 Ladysmith, British Columbia, V9G 1A5

                 (“Diamond”)


GIVEN THAT:

A.     Ladysmith is a municipality incorporated under the provisions of the Local Government
       Act;

B.     Ladysmith owns and operates the Ladysmith Water System to serve the Town of
       Ladysmith;

C.     Diamond is an Improvement District incorporated under the provisions of the Local
       Government Act;

D.     Diamond owns and operates the Diamond Water System to serve the Diamond
       Improvement District;

E.     Ladysmith and Diamond entered into an agreement for the supply of water by Ladysmith
       to Diamond dated October 2, 1995 that ended October 15, 2015 and since that date,
       Diamond has been paying Ladysmith the user rates payable under that agreement;

F.     This Agreement replaces the agreement referenced in Recital E and settles all outstanding
       issues with respect to the supply of water by Ladysmith to Diamond;

G.     Ladysmith has the authority to enter into an agreement with Diamond to provide water
       Services to Diamond under section 23 of the Community Charter;

H.     Ladysmith and Diamond wish to enter into this Agreement to set out the terms and
       conditions under which Ladysmith will provide the water service to Diamond;

NOW THEREFORE, this Agreement witnesses that in consideration of the premises and of the
mutual covenants and Agreements contained in this Agreement, the Parties agree as follows:

1.0     DEFINITIONS AND INTERPRETATION

Definitions

1.1    In this Agreement,

      (a)    “Bulk Meter” means a bulk water service meter to measure the total water supplied
             as part of the Services, and includes any ancillary vault structure;

      (b)    “Business Day” means any day except Saturdays, Sundays and British Columbia
             statutory holidays;

      (c)    “Community Charter” means the Community Charter, SBC 2003, c. 26;

      (d)    “Connection” means those parts of the Works that connect the Ladysmith Water
             System to the Diamond Water System

      (e)    “DCC Costs Equivalent Charge” means the charge for water treatment and supply
             from the Ladysmith Water System required to be paid by Diamond to Ladysmith
             under Part 5 of this Agreement;

      (f)    “Development Cost Charges Bylaw” means Ladysmith’s Development Cost Charges
             Bylaw, 2011, No. 1762;

      (g)    “Diamond Water System” means the Water System owned and operated by
             Diamond, and, with the exception of the Bulk Meters and Connections, located within
             the boundaries of Diamond as detailed in the map attached as Schedule A;

      (h)    “Director of Infrastructure Services” means the individual designated by
             Ladysmith’s Council as the Director of Infrastructure Services, or individuals
             designated by the Council from time to time to act in the place of him or her;

      (i)    “Event of Default” means an event described in Section 14.1;

      (j)    “Force Majeure” means an act of God, act of Canada’s enemies, sabotage, war,
             blockades, insurrections, riots, epidemics, lighting, earthquakes, floods, storms, fires,
             washouts, nuclear and radiation activity or fall out, arrests and distraints of rulers and
             people, civil disturbances, explosion, expropriation, or any act, omission or event
             whether of the kind enumerated in this definition or otherwise not within the control
             of a Party, which by the exercise of reasonable due diligence, the Party could not
             have prevented;

      (k)    “Ladysmith Water System” means the Water System owned and operated by

2.0   PROVISION OF WATER SERVICES

2.1    Subject to the terms and conditions of this Agreement, Ladysmith agrees to supply bulk
       water to Diamond up to the following amounts for the corresponding periods:

       Year                                   Amount

       July 1, 2016 – June 30, 2017           70,000 cubic meters

       July 1, 2017 – June 30, 2018           70,000 cubic meters

       July 1, 2018 – June 30, 2019           70,000 cubic meters

       July 1, 2019 – June 30, 2020           70,000 cubic meters

       July 1, 2020 – June 30, 2021           70,000 cubic meters.


{00383911; 9 }

--- Page 39 ---

                                                                                       Page 5 of 18



2.2    The Parties acknowledge and agree that while Ladysmith is not obligated to supply more
       water than the amounts detailed in Section 2.1, actual amounts of water supplied by
       Ladysmith under this Agreement may exceed those amounts and Diamond shall be
       obligated to pay for any excess water supplied in accordance with Section 3.1.

2.3   Ladysmith shall provide the Service from the Ladysmith Water System to the Diamond
      Water System at the Connections.

2.4    Ladysmith owns the Ladysmith Water System and shall be solely responsible for its
       construction, repair, replacement and maintenance, at its sole cost.

2.5   Diamond owns the Diamond Water System and shall be solely responsible for its
      construction, repair, replacement and maintenance, at its sole cost.

3.0   RATES AND PAYMENT

3.1    The parties agree that Diamond shall pay Ladysmith for the Services at a rate of $0.62 per
       cubic meter of water supplied to Diamond, for the Term.

3.2    In addition to the amount payable under Section 3.1, Diamond shall pay to Ladysmith:

      (a)    the Parcel Tax Equivalent in accordance with Part 4;

      (b)    the DCC Costs Equivalent Charges in accordance with Part 5;

      (c)    any costs incurred by Ladysmith under Section 10.6; and

      (d)    interest in respect of arrears of payments owing, in accordance with Section 3.6.

3.3    Diamond shall pay the amount owing under Section 3.1 and Subsection 3.2(a) quarterly.
       Ladysmith shall invoice Diamond for the amounts owing and Diamond shall pay to
       Ladysmith the amount invoiced within thirty (30) days of the date of the invoice. The
       invoice shall set out the details of the calculation used to determine the amount owing for
       the prior quarter.

3.4    Diamond shall pay the amount owing under Subsection 3.2(b) in accordance with Section
       5.4.

3.5    In respect of the payments due and owing under Subsections 3.2 (c) and (d), Ladysmith
       shall invoice Diamond when amounts become due and owing under this Agreement and
       Diamond shall pay to Ladysmith the amount invoiced within thirty (30) days of the date of
       the invoice. The invoice shall set out the details of the calculation used to determine the
       amount owing.

3.6    Overdue payments owing by Diamond to Ladysmith under this Agreement shall bear
       interest at a rate of ten percent (10%) per year, calculated annually.


{00383911; 9 }

--- Page 40 ---

                                                                                       Page 6 of 18


3.7    If a Party has a concern with the amounts paid or invoiced under this Agreement, the Party
       may request a review of amounts payable, and the Parties shall meet as soon as reasonably
       possible and attempt to resolve the concerns. The Parties may implement the process in
       Part 14 if necessary. In connection with such review, the Parties shall each provide such
       documentation and disclosure as is reasonably necessary to calculate and confirm amounts
       paid or payable under this Part.

4.0   PARCEL TAX EQUIVALENT

4.1   Without limiting amounts due and owing under other provisions of this Agreement,
      Diamond shall pay Ladysmith the Parcel Tax Equivalent quarterly as provided in Section
      4.2.

4.2   The Parcel Tax Equivalent payable by Diamond to Ladysmith shall be the amount equal to
      80% of the water parcel tax payable for a parcel under Ladysmith’s Water Parcel Tax
      Bylaw on July 1 of each year of the Term, multiplied by the number of Parcels in Diamond
      on that date and divided by four to determine the amount to be paid quarterly for the
      following twelve months.

5.0   DCC COSTS EQUIVALENT

5.1   Without limiting amounts due and owing under other provisions of this Agreement,
      Diamond shall collect and pay to Ladysmith a DCC Costs Equivalent Charge for water
      treatment and supply, for each new Parcel or new dwelling connected to the Water System
      during the Term, as provided in Sections 5.2 to 5.4 below, as a condition of supplying
      water to the new Parcel or dwelling, as the case may be.

5.2   The DCC Costs Equivalent Charge shall be an amount equal to the Development Cost
      Charge established for water under Ladysmith’s Development Cost Charges Bylaw that
      would apply to the same class of development for the Services if the development were
      within Ladysmith.

5.3   Diamond shall collect the DCC Costs Equivalent Charge as follows:

      (a)    at the time of subdivision approval, a DCC Costs Equivalent Charge shall be charged
             and collected from the subdivision applicant for each Parcel created by the
             subdivision;

      (b)    at the time of building permit issuance for the construction of a dwelling, including a
             secondary suite in an existing dwelling, a DCC Costs Equivalent Charge shall be
             charged and collected from the owner of the Parcel,

      provided that a DCC Costs Equivalent Charge shall not be charged and is not payable
      where a Development Cost Charge would not be payable under the Development Cost
      Charges Bylaw if the development were in Ladysmith, including where the DCC Costs
      Equivalent Charge has been previously paid on the same development.



{00383911; 9 }

--- Page 41 ---

                                                                                     Page 7 of 18


5.4   Diamond shall pay the DCC Costs Equivalent Charge to Ladysmith forthwith when
      Diamond collects each DCC Costs Equivalent Charge, in each year of the Term of this
      Agreement. Ladysmith acknowledges and agrees that Diamond is not involved in building
      permitting, and intends to collect the DCC Costs Equivalent Charge- if it was not collected
      at subdivision approval- at the time a land owner requests the installation of the water
      metre required for a dwelling, which is typically close to the time of building permit
      issuance.

5.5   Without limiting Section 8.6, the Parties shall undertake an annual reconciliation and
      adjustment of the DCC Costs Equivalent Charges payable under this Part 5 in each year of
      the Term of this Agreement, which shall be completed by February 28 each year for the
      preceding year. In connection with such reconciliation and adjustment, the Parties shall
      each provide such documentation and disclosure as is reasonably necessary to calculate and
      confirm the DCC Costs Equivalent Charges and in connection with this documentation and
      disclosure, Diamond shall provide a detailed report to Ladysmith of all subdivisions
      approved and construction of dwellings within Diamond in the preceding year. Any
      disagreements or disputes respecting the determination of amounts payable under this Part
      5 shall be resolved in accordance with the procedures set out in Part 14.

6.0   WATER QUALITY, QUANTITY AND SERVICE INTERRUPTIONS

6.1   The water supplied to Diamond by Ladysmith shall be of substantially the same quality as
      water provided to other users of the Ladysmith Water System. Ladysmith shall
      immediately notify Diamond of any water quality issues or concerns that arise during the
      Term, provide to Diamond a copy of any water quality testing results related to that
      concern, take all steps reasonably necessary to resolve any water quality concerns as soon
      as possible after such a concern is identified, and shall keep Diamond informed of the steps
      being taken and the anticipated timeline for resolution.

6.2   Ladysmith shall provide the Services at the same level or degree to which water services
      are provided elsewhere within Ladysmith. Ladysmith makes no representation or warranty
      that the level or degree of the Services provided under this Agreement will be maintained
      or continued to any particular standard, other than as stated expressly herein. For greater
      certainty, in the event that the Ladysmith is subject to water restrictions, Diamond agrees
      that the same water restrictions will also apply to Diamond and Diamond shall take all
      reasonable and necessary actions to effect those water restrictions within the Diamond
      Improvement District.

6.3   Ladysmith represents and warrants that the water provided under this Agreement meets
      British Columbia drinking water guidelines at the Connections, and Diamond agrees that it
      is responsible for ensuring that water distributed within the Diamond Water System shall
      also meet British Columbia drinking water guidelines through the point of delivery to its
      customers.

6.4   Diamond acknowledges and agrees that there may be from time to time interruptions or
      reductions in the level of the Services, and that Ladysmith shall not be held liable for any


{00383911; 9 }

--- Page 42 ---

                                                                                        Page 8 of 18


      losses, costs, damages, claims or expenses arising from or connected with a temporary
      interruption or reduction in the level of the Services provided under this Agreement.

6.5    Ladysmith shall provide Diamond with at least fifteen (15) days advance notice of all
       planned interruptions to the Services, and shall advise Diamond immediately of all
       unplanned interruptions. Ladysmith shall use best efforts to minimize all planned
       interruptions, and to ensure that planned and unplanned service interruptions are addressed
       as quickly as possible in order to restore the Services as expeditiously as reasonably
       possible. Ladysmith shall provide periodic updates to Diamond during all service
       interruptions respecting the anticipated timeframe for restoring the Services.

7.0   REPRESENTATIONS AND WARRANTIES

7.1    Each Party represents and warrants to the other as follows:

      (a)    it has the power and capacity to enter into this Agreement;

      (b)    this Agreement is valid and binding on it in accordance with its terms;

      (c)    the performance of its obligations under this Agreement does not breach the terms of
             any other agreement or obligation to which it is a party; and

      (d)    it now holds and will hold its Water System beneficially and free and clear of all
             restrictions, liens, encumbrances, floating charges or financial obligations of any kind
             except:

             (i)    the obligations created under this Agreement; or

             (ii)   as agreed between the Parties from time to time.

8.0   TERM AND TERMINATION
8.1   This Agreement takes effect on the Reference Date and is for a term of five (5) years,
      ending on June 30, 2021, unless terminated earlier in accordance with this Agreement.

8.2    At least one (1) year prior to the end of the Term, the Parties shall negotiate and make best
       efforts to reach agreement on an extension or replacement of this Agreement.

8.3    The Parties may terminate this Agreement by mutual agreement.

8.4    A Party may terminate this Agreement by providing at least six (6) month’s written notice
       to the other Party if there has been an Event of Default that has not been resolved through
       the dispute resolution process set out in Part 14, or the Parties are unable to amend this
       Agreement in accordance with Section 16.2.




{00383911; 9 }

--- Page 43 ---

                                                                                       Page 9 of 18


8.5    Despite any other provisions of this Agreement, neither Party may terminate this
       Agreement during any attempt to resolve issues through the dispute resolution process set
       out in Part 14.

8.6    If this Agreement is terminated or comes to an end, there shall be a reconciliation and final
       adjustment of amounts owing by Diamond to Ladysmith under Part 3, calculated up to the
       date of termination, and the obligation to make any adjusting payment shall survive the
       termination of this Agreement.

8.7    If Ladysmith continues to provide the Services to Diamond following the Term without
       any further written agreement, the terms and conditions set out in this Agreement,
       including all amounts payable under Part 3, shall continue to apply on a month to month
       basis until a new agreement is made or the Services are terminated, whichever occurs first,
       provided that the user rate payable under section 3.1 shall be equivalent to 90% of the rate
       then applicable for residential users in Ladysmith.

9.0   AREA AND CONNECTION TO THE LADYSMITH WATER SYSTEM

9.1    There is no restriction under this Agreement as to the areas within Diamond that may be
       connected to the Diamond Water System, provided that Diamond agrees that the Services
       shall not be resold, connected or provided to any person or entity, directly or indirectly,
       other than to a Parcel, person or entity within the boundaries of Diamond.

9.2    During the Term, Diamond agrees to notify Ladysmith of any change in the boundaries of
       Diamond.

9.3    Diamond agrees not to supply or provide the Diamond Water System with any source of
       water other than the water provided by Ladysmith under this Agreement, unless otherwise
       agreed by the Parties in writing.

9.4    The Parties acknowledge that the supply of water by Ladysmith to Diamond is currently
       supplied by two Connections between the Ladysmith Water System and the Diamond
       Water System as shown in Schedule A.

9.5 The Parties acknowledge and agree that the locations of Connections existing on the
     Reference Date are acceptable to both parties. Ladysmith agrees that it shall not require the
     relocation of existing Connections without first consulting with Diamond and if it requires
     relocation Diamond shall be responsible for all risk and costs associated with such
     relocation.

9.6    The maintenance, repair and replacement, if necessary, of the Connections shall be at the
       sole expense of Diamond.

9.7    Subject to Section 9.8, Diamond may construct, install and use one or more additional
       Connections if:

      (a)    Diamond pays for all costs related to designing, financing, constructing, installing,

      (c)    before commencing construction of an additional Connection, Diamond submits all

10.0 METERING

10.1 The Parties acknowledge and agree that the locations of the two (2) Bulk Meters existing
     on the Reference Date are acceptable to Ladysmith and the Director of Infrastructure
     Services. Ladysmith agrees that it shall not require the relocation of the existing Bulk
     Meters without first consulting with Diamond and shall not require the replacement of a
     Bulk Meter that is operational without first consulting with Diamond.

10.2 The Parties agree that Diamond is responsible for the installation, operation, maintenance,
     repair, and replacement if necessary, of the Bulk Meters. Ladysmith hereby grants to
     Diamond a non-exclusive license to access and occupy the locations of the Bulk Meters at
     all times during the Term, for these purposes.

10.3 Ladysmith shall measure the water flow from the Ladysmith Water System to the Diamond
     Water System by reading each Bulk Meter and adding together the amount from each Bulk
     Meter to determine the total amount of water used by Diamond.

10.4 Either Ladysmith or Diamond at its sole cost may at any time appoint a qualified
     representative to ascertain the accuracy of any Bulk Meter used in connection with this
     Agreement.

10.5 Ladysmith shall notify Diamond of any repairs or maintenance that it determines are
     required to the Bulk Meter or the Connections, and on being notified Diamond shall take

11.0 ON-GOING COMMUNICATIONS

11.1 Each Party shall, within ten (10) days of the commencement of this Agreement, appoint a

     and provide contact information for that person to the other party.

11.2 The representatives shall

      (a)    oversee the implementation of this Agreement and the delivery of the Services;

      (b)    meet as needed to review and discuss any issues arising under this Agreement;

      (c)    each be available and respond in a timely manner to an inquiry from the other
             representative respecting this Agreement;

      (d)    review and attempt to resolve any Service delivery issues that arise from time to time,
             including Service interruptions;

      (e)    consider and recommend amendments to this Agreement to address changes in
             circumstances or other issues that arise; and

      (f) each bring forward issues and concerns as necessary with their respective Council and
            Board of Trustees for input and direction.

13.0 RECORDS

13.1 Each Party shall cause all books and records with respect to this Agreement and its Water
     System to be kept in its offices. Each Party shall permit the other Party, its accountants and
     other representatives, at the other Party’s own expense and at all reasonable times to
     examine and make copies of any and all documents under the control of a Party and
     relating to this Agreement.

14.0 DEFAULT AND DISPUTE RESOLUTION

14.1 The occurrence of any of the following events shall be an Event of Default under this
     Agreement:

      (a)    the failure of a Party to perform or observe any of its covenants or agreements in this
             Agreement, if such failure is not cured within 45 days of written notice from the other
             Party specifying such failure, or if full compliance is not possible for reasons beyond
             a Party’s control, a failure to provide the other Party with a plan and schedule of
             compliance and to proceed diligently with the plan in accordance with the schedule;
      (b)    a Party:

             (i)      becomes insolvent; or

             (ii)     acknowledges its insolvency;

      (c)    a statutory trustee or provincial agent is appointed in respect of any property or asset
             of a Party and is not discharged within 45 days; or

      (d)    Diamond fails to pay Ladysmith any of the amounts payable under this Agreement,
             within three (3) months of written notice to Diamond of failure to pay.


14.2 If the Parties are unable to agree on the interpretation or application of any provision in the
     Agreement, if there is an Event of Default, or if the Parties are unable to resolve any other
     issue relating to this Agreement, the Parties agree to the following process in the order it is
     set out:

       (a)       the Party initiating the process shall send written notice to the other Party;

       (b)       the Parties shall promptly, diligently and in good faith take all reasonable measures
                 to negotiate an acceptable resolution to the disagreement or dispute;

       (c)       if the Parties are unable to negotiate a resolution under paragraph (b) within thirty
                 (30) Business Days, the parties may, by agreement, appoint a mutually acceptable
                 person to mediate the matter, and the parties must act reasonably and in good faith
                 and cooperate with the mediator and with each other in an attempt to resolve the
                 matter within thirty (30) Business Days after the mediator is appointed. The costs of



{00383911; 9 }

--- Page 48 ---

                                                                                           Page 14 of 18


                 the mediator and any costs of facilities shall be shared equally by the parties; and

       (d)       if the Parties do not implement mediation under paragraph (c) or are unable to
                 resolve the dispute if mediation under paragraph (c) is implemented, either Party may
                 give notice to the other Party that the matter shall be decided by binding arbitration.

14.3     Where notice is given under Section 14.2(d), a single arbitrator shall be appointed by
         agreement within sixty (60) Business Days of the notice, and if the Parties are unable to
         agree within that time, the arbitrator shall be appointed by the British Columbia
         International Commercial Arbitration Centre. The arbitration shall follow the rules of the
         Arbitration Act, RSBC 1996 c. 55 unless the Parties agree otherwise, and the decision of
         the arbitrator is final, binding and conclusive.

14.4 Unless otherwise agreed by the Parties or ordered by an arbitrator, each Party shall pay its
     own legal and other costs, and shall share equally the costs for an arbitrator and any
     required facilities.

14.5 No Party shall be liable for its failure to perform any of its obligations under this
     Agreement due to Force Majeure.

15.0 APPROVALS

15.1 This Agreement is subject to the following approvals and shall come into effect only after
     both of these approvals are obtained:

       (a)   the municipal Council of Ladysmith shall have approved this Agreement and satisfied
             all of its statutory obligations under the Community Charter, Local Government Act
             and other applicable enactment; and

       (b)   the Board of Trustees of Diamond shall have approved this Agreement and satisfied
             all of its statutory obligations under the Local Government Act and other applicable
             enactments.

16.0 AMENDMENTS

16.1 This Agreement may not be modified or amended except by written agreement duly
     authorized by the Parties.

16.2 If any laws of Canada or British Columbia are promulgated, amended or repealed, such that
     substantial portions of the Agreement are no longer effective or incapable of being
     performed in the opinion of Diamond or Ladysmith, acting reasonably, the Parties agree to
     use their reasonable best efforts to negotiate such amendments to this Agreement as are
     necessary to give effect to the intention of the Parties under this Agreement. Should
     negotiations fail to result in an agreement being reached within one year of the date of the
     first meeting, either Party shall have the option of terminating this Agreement in
     accordance with Section 8.4.

17.0 NOTICES

17.1 Any notice or other communication under this Agreement shall be in writing and shall be
     given by the delivery or rendering thereof to its addressee by hand, by prepaid first class
     mail, by email or by facsimile transmission, to the contact information below:

17.2    A notice or other communication so given shall be deemed to have been received at the
        time of its delivery if delivered by hand, three (3) Business Days after the date of mailing
        if mailed, if by email or fax, on the next Business Day after it is transmitted. Each Party
        shall notify the other Party of any change of contact information.

18.0 MISCELLANEOUS

Entire Agreement

18.1 This Agreement is the entire agreement between the parties respecting its subject matter
     and there are no undertakings, representations or promises, express or implied, other than
     those expressly set out in this Agreement.

Agreement for Services

18.2 This Agreement is an agreement for the provision of services, and nothing in this
     Agreement is intended to be or shall be interpreted as creating a partnership, agency or
     joint venture relationship of any kind between the Parties, or as imposing on either Party a
     partnership duty, liability or obligation of any kind in relation to the other Party.

Enurement

18.3 This Agreement shall be binding upon and enure to the benefit of the Parties and their
     respective successors and permitted assigns.

Further Assurances

18.4 Each Party shall perform any act and execute and deliver any document reasonably
     required by any other Party to carry out the terms of this Agreement in accordance with its
     true intent and meaning.

Statutory Obligations and Powers Preserved

18.5 The obligations of the Parties under this Agreement are always subject to the Community
     Charter, Local Government Act, and other applicable enactments and the Parties shall
     abide by all applicable enactments in carrying out the terms of this Agreement. Except as
     specifically provided, nothing contained or implied in this Agreement will impair or affect
     the Parties’ rights and powers in the exercise of their functions pursuant to the Community
     Charter, the Local Government Act or any other enactment.

No Assignment

18.6 Neither this Agreement nor any part of it may be assigned by either Party without the
     written consent of the other Party.

Consents and Waivers

18.7 No consent or waiver, express or implied, by either Party of any breach or default by the
     other under this Agreement shall:

      (a)    be valid unless it is in writing and stated to be a consent or waiver pursuant to this
             Section;

      (b)    be relied on as a consent to or waiver of any other breach or default of the same or
             any other nature;

      (c)    constitute a general waiver under this Agreement; or

      (d)    eliminate or modify the need for a specific consent or waiver under this Section in
             any other or subsequent instance.

Time of the Essence

18.8 Time is of the essence in the performance of each obligation under this Agreement.

Survival on Termination

18.9 The provisions of this Agreement necessary to give full effect thereto shall survive the
